qs.q: A hospitalized patient is prescribed a carbapenem that requires once-daily dosing but notably lacks activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter. Which drug is this?
qs.e: Ertapenem is administered once daily but is famous for the 'Ertapenem trap' of missing Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter coverage. Meropenem and doripenem reliably cover Pseudomonas.

qs.q: Which fluoroquinolone possesses excellent activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and is considered the best antipseudomonal quinolone in its class?
qs.e: Ciprofloxacin is the most potent quinolone against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Moxifloxacin undergoes hepatic elimination and is not used for urinary tract infections or Pseudomonas.

qs.q: Which of the following β-lactam antibiotics is active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa?
qs.e: Piperacillin is an extended-spectrum penicillin with anti-pseudomonal activity. It's often combined with tazobactam (a β-lactamase inhibitor) for broader coverage. Pseudomonas requires specific β-lactams with structural features allowing penetration through its outer membrane porins.
qs.s: Basic Pharmacology - Study Guide — MCQ Bank

qs.q: Green-blue pus with a fruity odor in a burn patient is characteristic of an infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The green color is due to pyocyanin and the fruity odor is due to pyrazinamide production.
qs.e: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen often associated with hospital-acquired infections, particularly in burn patients. It is known for producing characteristic pigments like pyocyanin (blue-green) and elastase, which contribute to the color and odor of the wound exudate.

qs.q: A 72-year-old man is admitted to the hospital from a nursing home with severe pneumonia. He was discharged from the hospital 1 week ago after open heart surgery. The patient has no known allergies. Which of the following regimens is most appropriate for empiric coverage of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in this patient?
qs.e: This patient is at high risk for healthcare-associated pneumonia (HAP) with resistant pathogens. Vancomycin provides MRSA coverage, and piperacillin-tazobactam provides broad-spectrum Gram-negative coverage, including Pseudomonas. Levofloxacin alone may not adequately cover MRSA, and ceftriaxone/azithromycin is insufficient for MRSA and Pseudomonas.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Microbiology Exam - May 29, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which of the following statements regarding Pseudomonas aeruginosa is correct?
o: It is characterized by its inability to grow in the presence of oxygen.
It is a common cause of opportunistic infections in immunocompromised individuals.
It is an obligate intracellular pathogen requiring host cells for replication.
It is most commonly acquired through ingestion of contaminated food sources.
qs.e: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic, Gram-negative rod that is ubiquitous in the environment. It frequently causes infections in patients with weakened immune systems, such as those with cystic fibrosis, burns, or prolonged hospitalization, often in healthcare settings.

ai.subject: Microbiology & immunology
ai.summary: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a gram‑negative rod that thrives in moist environments and forms biofilms. It causes opportunistic infections, especially in immunocompromised or device‑bearing patients. Rapid recognition and appropriate antibiotics are essential.

sections.p: P. aeruginosa is a ubiquitous, aerobic, gram‑negative rod with a distinctive grape‑like odor. It is intrinsically resistant to many antibiotics and can form protective biofilms on surfaces and devices.
b: Gram‑negative rod; oxidase positive; motile; produces pyocyanin pigment

sections.p: Its virulence stems from exotoxins, elastases, and a robust biofilm matrix that shields it from host defenses and antibiotics.
b: Biofilm – protects against immune cells and drugs

sections.p: The bacterium survives in water, soil, and hospital sinks. It spreads via contaminated equipment, hands, or environmental surfaces.

P. aeruginosa causes a spectrum of infections: ventilator‑associated pneumonia, catheter‑related bloodstream infections, burn wound sepsis, and ocular infections. In cystic fibrosis, chronic airway colonization leads to progressive lung damage.
Clinical suspicion is followed by culture and susceptibility testing. In low‑resource settings, a simple Gram stain and growth on cetrimide agar can suggest the organism.
b: Sputum or wound culture on cetrimide agar

t.b: Shows gram‑negative rods; suggests Pseudomonas if oxidase positive
Mucoid colonies indicate Pseudomonas; confirms identity when available

sections.p: First treat the source (remove catheters, decontaminate surfaces). Use antipseudomonal beta‑lactams or fluoroquinolones, avoiding agents with poor penetration or high toxicity.
b: Avoid aminoglycosides alone due to nephrotoxicity

t.b: Removal of infected device reduces bacterial load
Check renal function when using nephrotoxic agents

sections.p: Remember that Pseudomonas is a common cause of infection in patients with indwelling devices, burns, or cystic fibrosis. Its biofilm formation explains chronicity and resistance.
Other gram‑negative rods like Acinetobacter or Klebsiella can cause similar hospital infections but lack the characteristic odor and pigment.
b: Acinetobacter – no grape odor; Klebsiella – lactose fermenter

sections.p: Low‑yield cultures in early infection may miss Pseudomonas; a negative Gram stain does not rule it out. Biofilm‑producing strains may show delayed growth.

faq.q: What makes Pseudomonas resistant to many antibiotics?
faq.a: It has efflux pumps, low‑permeability outer membrane, and enzymes that inactivate beta‑lactams.

faq.q: Can it be prevented in hospitals?
faq.a: Strict hand hygiene, equipment sterilization, and limiting unnecessary catheter use reduce spread.

faq.q: Why does it cause green sputum?
faq.a: The pigment pyocyanin gives a greenish hue to secretions.

exam: Explain why Pseudomonas is a common pathogen in ventilator‑associated pneumonia and describe the first‑line treatment strategy.
